input.title: ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
input.bodyText:
ZM3D playable - brief for PlayableX
Zombie Match 3D (Puzzles vs Zombies). Written 1 October 2025 by Julia Lawson for the build as it is today. If we change the core gameplay before the start, we will redo the affected parts of this brief with you in November.

1. Start date
Kickoff: Monday 3 November 2025. Everything still owed from our side is on the hand-off list (linked below) and in the PlayableX channel.

2. Scenario and what it is for
We picked Scenario 1: the playable is the core game in its simplest form. The goal is retention, not cheapest CPI. It should filter out people who won't enjoy the real game and stay true to how it plays. The player picks items freely from the pile and can make as many matches as they are good enough to make. It is not on rails.

3. How the level plays (from the design page and the reference level deck)
- 3D items sit in a physics pile. The player taps or drags items into a tray at the bottom.
- The tray has 7 slots. Three matching items in the tray clear, and the matched set is fired at the zombies by the cannon (the "rocket launcher") with its projectile.
- Zombies walk towards us across the battlefield. Different items hit differently: the grenade is powerful, the couch does splash damage, and the plushie is weak but funny.
- Win: every zombie on screen is eliminated.
- Lose: the zombies reach us and our HP runs out.
- Filling all 7 slots without a match is a blunder, not a loss. The tray clears and the surviving zombies enrage, but play continues. The loss screen only comes at zero HP.
- Reference: "ZM3D playable - reference level" deck (built 23 Sep, recorded by Brian) and the background of that level.

4. The board: eight items
The default board is these eight:
- Grenade
- Couch
- Plushie Chick (the "duck" in the reference level)
- Shuriken
- Cute Axe
- Gift Box
- Cactus Plant
- Dynamite
Every other board item on the hand-off list is an extra you can swap in on the editable board.

5. Zombies and animation
Four zombies: Party Girl, Plumber, Magician, Football Player. All four are in the Unity package Marcus sent on 26 Sep.
One animation: walk, applied to all four for the Spine re-rig.

6. Sound
We only hand over sound that is ours.
- Ours, and yours to use: matching sound, success sound, failure sound, and the background music (a new track made for the ad, not the in-game track; Calvin is still cutting it to a loop).
- Not ours yet: the rocket sound (Soundly library) and the explosion sound (bought Unity Asset Store pack). These stay with us until Calvin has made our own versions, and we will send those when ready. Please don't use library sounds in the meantime.
- Music may only start after the player's first click (your rule from the Domino Delights playable).

7. Formats (as you gave them to us)
- 3D: .fbx, .glb or .blend. FBX exported in Binary, not ASCII.
- 2D: .png. For 2D animation, character parts are separated into pieces.
- Font: .ttf or .woff2
- Sound: .mp3 or .wav

8. What is still coming from us
The hand-off list sheet has one row per line of the pack. Delivered means you already have the current file. Ready means it is exported in one of your formats, sits in our outgoing folder, opens, and is the current version. Owed means we still owe it, and the sheet says what and who has it. Owed lines include Cactus Plant from the default board (new pot colours and a revised model), the bathroom set (being re-UV'd), the rocket and explosion sounds, the background music, item visuals, UI elements and fonts.

Contacts: Julia Lawson (brief, design), Brian Foster (asset pack), Frederick Stone (project owner).

text:
Done. Where the pack stands today, across all 96 lines of Brian's list:
• *Delivered: 8* (Couch, Couch and Pillow, Grenade, Plushie Bunny, Plushie Chick, Cannon, Background, the zombie pack)
• *Ready: 56*
• *Owed: 32*

Of the 8 board items, 3 are delivered, 4 are ready, and 1 is owed: Cactus Plant. Claire revised it after Brian exported it, then made new pot colours on the 29th, so it has to go again. Chainsaw and Cone are in the same position.
Other things that changed since Brian's notes:
• The 12 bathroom files Claire gave Brian on Friday are the old version, because she's redoing their UVs (per Robert).
• Rocket and explosion sounds come from a library and a bought pack, so they stay here until Calvin makes our own.
Who owes what: Claire 20, Brian 8, Calvin 3, Martin 1 (fonts).

The 32 Owed tickets are in Todo, each with a comment. Both files are view-only for you, Brian, Robert and PlayableX intake.
Brief: https://docs.google.com/document/d/61545827e5f4fa04d431927b/edit

Hi <@PERSON_6078_SLACK_ID>, ahead of the 3 November start, here is the brief to build from and the list of what's still coming from us. Both are also shared with intake@playablex.ai.
• Brief (Scenario 1, the 8 board items, 4 zombies with walk, win/lose and the 7-slot tray, sound, music after the first click): https://docs.google.com/document/d/61545827e5f4fa04d431927b/edit
• Hand-off list, one row per asset: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/15LDL7BC6GpYJfVCLBL-qgL51Ago7wQWiDdzQkVr_2Gw/edit

Status today: 8 delivered, 56 ready to send, 32 still owed. The owed items include Cactus Plant from the board set, the bathroom items, the rocket and explosion sounds, the background music, item visuals, UI elements and fonts. The brief covers the game as it plays today; if our core gameplay changes, we'll go through the affected parts with you in November.
Correction to the split: Claire owes 21 and Brian owes 7, not 20 and 8. Calvin 3 and Martin 1 are right, and the total is still 32.
